transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Riley Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Acme CISO), Tom Nguyen (Head of Infra), Sara Bell (Compliance)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- High-level SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture review for Redwood.
- Discussed Trust Center access, scope of reports, controls mapping, KMS/BYOK options, RBAC/SSO/SCIM, audit log retention and data residency.
- Next steps: share reports via Trust Center, provide controls mapping spreadsheet, schedule technical deep dive on encryption and VPC private deployment.

Topics:
- Trust Center access and where to get artifacts
- SOC 2 Type II scope and date
- ISO 27001 certificate and scope
- Controls mapping to Acme requirements
- Encryption, KMS/HSM, BYOK, and key rotation
- RBAC, SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning
- Audit logs, retention, and log export options
- Data residency and Private/Dedicated deployment options

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick off, uh, we're expecting about 45 minutes, Riley from our security engineering team is with me.
[00:06] Maya Lopez: great, thanks Jordan. Maya here, i'm the CISO at Acme Health. Tom and Sara are here as well. main aim today is to understand redwood's control evidence and how it maps to our SOC 2/ISO requirements, especially for patient-adjacent data.
[00:18] Jordan Patel: perfect, absolutely. Riley do you want to intro yourself?
[00:20] Riley Chen: sure, hi everyone, Riley Chen, Security Engineer, i own infra security and compliance integrations for redwood. i'll be technical lead on the follow-up for KMS and VPC details.
[00:29] Tom Nguyen: quick note, we have a tight timeline, our procurement needs evidence by end of feb for our vendor board. so if you can share artifacts quickly that helps.
[00:37] Jordan Patel: understood, we'll prioritize. quick agenda: 1) trust center and reports 2) scope & controls mapping 3) encryption/KMS and BYOK options 4) identity and audit logs 5) next steps. sound good?
[00:46] Maya Lopez: sounds good.

[02:15] Riley Chen: jumping in on Trust Center — we host the SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate in our Trust Center. for third-party access we can either provide viewer links or a secure zip via our S3 presigned + short lived token. most customers request viewer links plus an NDA for full report download.
[02:34] Sara Bell: when was your last SOC 2 Type II audit? scope?
[02:38] Riley Chen: last Type II period ended 2024-11-30, so the report covers controls tested across july through november 2024. scope includes hosted api, dedicated, and private control plane — i'll double-check the exact systems in the report but that's the typical scope.
[02:53] Maya Lopez: does the SOC report cover encryption key management or is that a different attestation?
[02:58] Riley Chen: good q — SOC talks about control design and operating effectiveness, it references our encryption controls. for deep technical details we include KMS architecture notes and we also have an HSM/BYOK addendum for customers using private deployments.

[05:20] Tom Nguyen: we require BYOK with customer-managed keys and HSM-backed storage for any PHI adjacency. do you support an HSM integration in private deployments?
[05:27] Riley Chen: yes, for Private deployments we support HSM integrations and KMIP-compatible appliances, and our Dedicated offering can be configured with customer-managed keys in a cloud KMS or on-prem HSM depending on the deployment. open question is whether you'll need full on-prem key housing or cloud KMS with customer control.
[05:40] Sara Bell: what's the rotation policy? can we force rotate keys?
[05:43] Riley Chen: rotation is configurable. for BYOK we surface the rotation window and we can support forced rotation workflows; we'll include the specific API endpoints and automation steps in the follow-up doc.

[07:10] Jordan Patel: on ISO — we have an active ISO 27001 certificate, certified 2024, scope aligned with our hosted control plane and dedicated services. the certificate and statement of applicability are also in the Trust Center.
[07:22] Maya Lopez: good to hear. can you provide controls mapping? acme uses a mapping template where we map redwood's controls to acme's internal controls and to ISO/SOC requirements.
[07:31] Jordan Patel: yes, Riley will prepare a controls mapping spreadsheet — we'll map Redwood policies and controls to SOC 2 criteria and ISO annex A controls and then add notes about evidence artifacts and locations in Trust Center.

[09:00] Maya Lopez: about identity — we need SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for RBAC. our expectation is SSO with enforced 2FA and SCIM for user lifecycle. also service accounts should be limited and logged.
[09:13] Riley Chen: we support SAML 2.0, SSO with enforced MFA via IdP, and SCIM provisioning for account sync. RBAC is role-based with default roles and ability to create custom roles. all auth events are in our audit logs.
[09:29] Tom Nguyen: can logs be exported to our SIEM? we use Splunk with a secure forwarder.
[09:34] Riley Chen: yes, we support log export via secure syslog or push to cloud logging sinks (e.g., AWS Kinesis/CloudWatch, GCP Pub/Sub) and can provide an authenticated API for pulling logs. we will include retention windows and sample log formats in the follow-up.

[12:45] Sara Bell: what's the retention on audit logs in hosted environment? and can we extend retention on a per-customer basis?
[12:52] Riley Chen: default retention is 90 days for audit logs in hosted. for Dedicated/Private we can configure longer retention and ship logs to your archive. we also support real-time streaming to your SIEM so you can keep long term.

[15:10] Maya Lopez: on data residency — we operate in eu and us regions. our requirement is that data for eu patients remains in eu. does Redwood support region pinning and guarantees?
[15:22] Jordan Patel: yes, region pinning is supported; requests can be routed to eu-only deployment regions for hosted customers and Dedicated/Private can be provisioned in eu regions. our contracts include data residency commitments for dedicated capacity; we'll surface the exact language in the follow-up and in our Data Processing Agreement.

[17:00] Tom Nguyen: how do you handle backups and DR — encrypted backups, cross-region replication?
[17:05] Riley Chen: backups are encrypted at rest, keys are managed according to the chosen KMS mode (redwood-managed or customer-managed). cross-region replication is opt-in and encrypted in transit. for Private deployments on-prem, backups can be handled by customer tooling and we provide backup hooks.

[20:45] Maya Lopez: audit evidence — for procurement we'll need evidence of control operation: e.g., vulnerability scan cadence, patching windows, change control logs, penetration test reports. are pentest reports in the Trust Center?
[20:58] Riley Chen: we host summary pentest reports and an executive summary in the Trust Center. full redacted pentest reports are available under NDA. we also provide quarterly vulnerability scan summaries and our patch SLA for infra components.

[22:30] Sara Bell: about subservice organizations — we use a few cloud providers and there are dependencies there. does your SOC 2 carve those providers out or are they included as subservice orgs?
[22:41] Riley Chen: our SOC 2 includes AWS/GCP as subservice organizations and we provide related attestations as part of the mapping. we'll call out the exact vendor list in the controls mapping.

[25:10] Jordan Patel: question for acme — what level of detail do you need in the controls mapping? is a 1:1 map to your control IDs sufficient, or do you need evidence links and frequency notes?
[25:20] Maya Lopez: we need 1:1 mapping plus links to evidence and frequency/owner, that helps our audit team to validate.
[25:26] Jordan Patel: understood. we'll include owner and evidence link columns in the spreadsheet.

[28:00] Tom Nguyen: technical deep dive — we want to validate network layouts for VPC peering, private endpoints, and whether traffic for inference ever transits public internet in hosted mode.
[28:12] Riley Chen: in Hosted, control plane calls are over TLS and we use private networking where possible. inference traffic to GPU hosts may traverse our internal backbone; for strict network isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private where we colocate in your VPC or deploy a private control plane. we'll include network diagrams and a sample VPC design in the technical follow-up.

[31:40] Maya Lopez: one more compliance question — how do you handle evidence of employee background checks and access reviews?
[31:48] Jordan Patel: our HR and IAM controls are covered in SOC 2; we keep a record of background checks for employees with access to production systems. periodic access reviews and least privilege policies are documented; we'll point to the relevant sections in Trust Center.

[34:00] Sara Bell: can you support custom contractual clauses around security? e.g., specific incident notification SLA and subprocessor removal?
[34:09] Jordan Patel: we do negotiate some security addendum items at enterprise scale — incident notification SLA is standard, we can discuss subprocessor commitments; we'll route this to legal but can provide standard language and a path for custom clauses for enterprise terms.

[36:30] Riley Chen: quick note on monitoring — we provide metrics and traces per model/route in the console and can expose them via API; token-level logging is redacted by default but can be configured for debug under strict controls.

[38:50] Tom Nguyen: about token logging — we need assurance PHI won't be stored in logs or will be redacted. what's the default?
[38:58] Riley Chen: default is to not persist full user-provided prompt text in logs for hosted; we store metadata and truncated context. for customers that need full trace we have a strict opt-in with controls and retention policies; on Private you control log storage. we'll include redaction behavior and config flags in the follow-up.

[41:10] Jordan Patel: ok, quick recap and next steps: 1) Jordan will share Trust Center link and SOC 2 Type II + ISO artifacts by 2025-02-14. 2) Riley will produce a controls mapping spreadsheet and KMS/HSM integration notes by 2025-02-19. 3) we'll schedule a technical deep dive on VPC/KMS for the week of 2025-02-24. 4) Acme to share scoping doc and any must-have contractual clauses by 2025-02-18.
[41:41] Maya Lopez: that timeline works for us. appreciate the thoroughness.
[41:45] Jordan Patel: great — we'll follow up in email with links and the calendar invite. thanks everyone.
[41:50] Tom Nguyen: thanks all.
[41:52] Sara Bell: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

References shared during call: Trust Center (link placeholder), SOC 2 Type II (period ended 2024-11-30), ISO 27001 certificate (2024), Controls mapping template (will be shared), KMS/BYOK architecture doc (will be shared).
